newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian peso closes lower for seventh day.
newsitem.headline: Colombian peso closes lower for seventh day.

text.p: Colombia's peso closed lower for the seventh consecutive session, ending down 34 centavos at 997.99 in active trading on the country's interbank market.

Dealers said the peso looked set to break its losing streak at one point in early in the session when a flood of export dollars entered the market. But traders said the central bank ensured that the peso stayed within its daily floating rate band by buying about $9 million at 997.99 to the dollar.
The bank has a policy of not commenting on its interventions in the interbank market.

The central bank has been under growing pressure to devalue the peso, which has risen sharply since June, to help make Colombian exports more competitive abroad and boost the real value of export reveneues.
Dealers reported an above-average 211 trades in Tuesday's session and said the peso held in a 997.97 to 998.25 range.
